title: Charter Communications Q3 Results: Revenue Rises to $14.92 Billion as Impairment Drives Loss
excerpt: Reported revenue rose 9.1% on the Cox deal, but a $6.33 billion franchise impairment swung Charter to a $2.4 billion loss; on a pro forma basis revenue fell 1.5% as Internet losses widened to 233,000.
body:
• Charter Communications reported third-quarter revenue of $14.92 billion on an actual basis, up 9.1% year over year, driven by the Cox Communications transactions that closed on August 19, according to the company's release.
  • On a pro forma basis, treating Cox as owned for the full period, revenue fell 1.5% to $16.5 billion, and a $6.33 billion non-cash franchise impairment swung Charter to a net loss of $2.4 billion, or a diluted loss of $20.50 per share.
  • Spectrum lost 233,000 Internet customers on a pro forma basis, ending the quarter with 34.3 million, while Spectrum Mobile added 508,000 lines to reach 13.5 million, the company reported.
  • Charter announced a new operating model targeting $2 billion in annualized expense savings over 18 months, in addition to more than $1 billion in planned Cox synergies.

Two sets of numbers, one story

Charter Communications reported third-quarter results for the period ended September 30, 2026, before the market opened on Friday, November 6 — and the headline figures need the Cox deal to make sense. Charter completed its acquisition of Cox Communications on August 19, so actual results include Cox only from August 20 through September 30, the company said in its results release. On that actual basis, revenue rose 9.1% to $14.92 billion from $13.67 billion a year earlier.

The like-for-like picture is weaker: on a pro forma basis, as if Cox had been owned throughout both periods, revenue fell 1.5% to $16.5 billion, the company reported.

The impairment behind the loss

Charter posted a net loss attributable to shareholders of $2.4 billion on an actual basis, against net income of $1.14 billion a year earlier, and a GAAP diluted loss of $20.50 per share against earnings of $8.34 a year earlier, according to the release. The driver was a $6.33 billion non-cash franchise impairment charge, which the company linked to a sustained decline in its share price, partly offset by a gain of about $1.4 billion on debt extinguishment.

Stripping out those non-recurring items, Zacks put Charter's adjusted earnings at $21.70 per share, above its $9.08 consensus estimate, with reported revenue of $14.92 billion also ahead of its estimate. Readers should keep the two profit figures separate: the GAAP loss is the reported result, while the adjusted figure is an analyst measure that excludes the impairment and the debt gain.

"We will return Charter to Internet customer growth and transform Charter into a simpler, faster, more agile organization."

— Chris Winfrey, President and CEO, Charter Communications

Internet losses widen, mobile grows

The operating pressure sits in broadband. Spectrum Internet customers fell by 233,000 on a pro forma basis in the quarter — 156,000 at legacy Charter and 77,000 at legacy Cox — a wider loss than the 171,000 decline a year earlier, leaving 34.3 million Internet customers, the company reported. Pro forma Internet revenue fell 3.7% to $7.1 billion amid the customer losses and pricing and packaging changes, Zacks reported.

Mobile remains the offset: Spectrum Mobile added 508,000 lines on a pro forma basis, taking total lines to 13.5 million, up 15.4% year over year, with mobile service revenue up 17.3% to $1.16 billion, according to the release and Zacks. Video losses narrowed to 77,000, ending at 13.8 million customers, and total customer relationships fell 238,000 to 36.7 million.

Cash, costs and the savings plan

Adjusted EBITDA rose 6.9% to $5.9 billion on an actual basis, helped by Cox, while pro forma adjusted EBITDA fell 4.0% to $6.6 billion, the company reported. Free cash flow was $674 million, down $947 million from a year earlier, on lower operating cash flow of $4.0 billion and one-time Cox-related costs; capital expenditures were $3.0 billion on an actual basis.

Alongside the results, Charter launched a new operating model targeting $2 billion in annualized expense savings over 18 months, in addition to more than $1 billion in expected Cox synergies, according to the release.

What to watch next

The test is whether the savings plan returns Spectrum to Internet customer growth. Broadband losses widened even as mobile grew, so the next two quarters of Internet net additions will show whether the new model is working.
